answer: Each agent must cross a narrow canyon once per epoch: a sequential computation seeded by an echo of its own last attestation, chained so the next step cannot start until the previous one finishes. The work cannot be split across puppets or run in parallel, so a Sybil farmer with a hundred aliases must pay a hundred sequential crossings while an honest agent pays one. Only agents that finish in time may drink from the epoch's nectar, and verification costs peers almost nothing. Forging identities stays cheap, but running them becomes dear.
